samples.summary:
No design doc records the new current-slide invariant, even though the canonical doc explicitly documents the analogous case and states the opposite conclusion.

`slides-native-undo.md` §"Presence and selection" (lines 241-246) already reasons about post-undo dangling references: "After undo/redo, the editor's local selection may reference an element id that the reverse op removed … handled by the view layer reconciling selection against `read()` on the `notifyChange` tick. No store change required." This change adds the *slide-level* counterpart — a new editor-owned invariant (`currentIndex` + `resolveCurrentSlide()` heals the cursor, discards anchored crop/text-edit/cell-selection, and now permits `currentId === undefined` on an emptied deck) — and updates no doc under `docs/design/`. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 and :58-60 require a feature/non-trivial change to write or update a design doc ("Update the existing doc when …"), and slides.md documents editor behaviour at finer granularity than this (e.g. the color-picker commit/record contract at slides.md:505-530). The natural homes are `slides-native-undo.md` §Presence and selection or `slides.md` §Editor UI / §Rendering pipeline; a fold-in, not a new parallel file. Only `docs/tasks/active/20260820-slides-undo-add-slide-current-{todo,lessons}.md` were added, which are task plans, not design docs.

samples.summary: The invariant is enforced only as a side effect of a *painting* frame, so the acceptance criterion "any removal of the current slide moves the cursor somewhere valid" holds only in hosts that drive `render()` and mark the renderer dirty on store change. `slides-view.tsx:1051` does (`store.onChange → editor.markDirty()` + RAF `editor.render()`), but the mobile edit host mounts the same editor with **no render loop and no `store.onChange → markDirty` wiring** (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/mobile-slides-view.tsx:376-447`; its `store.onChange` at :309 belongs to the view-mode renderer branch). There a peer delete / undo leaves `currentId` dangling indefinitely — and `getCurrentSlideId()` is read eagerly by presence broadcast (`slides-view.tsx:1080`), the toolbar, and the key rules (`editor.ts:1586`), any of which can observe the stale id before the next dirty frame. An eager, non-paint hook already exists and is used elsewhere in this package (`SlidesStore.onChange`, e.g. `layout-list-panel.ts:114`, `notes-panel.ts:110`); healing on that tick (or in a small `reconcileCursor()` called from both) would make the invariant host-independent instead of paint-dependent. Design-layer/spec-coverage concern, not a line-level bug.

Two competing cursor-move policies now coexist for the same user-visible event. The thumbnail panel's `Delete slide` picks "the first surviving slide *after* the anchor, else the last before it" (thumbnail-panel.ts:306-323) and then calls `setCurrentSlide`; the new heal picks the slide *before* the vanished index (`editor.ts:1552-1554`). So deleting the current slide via the panel lands after it, while the identical removal arriving from undo or a peer lands before it. The panel's hand fix-up is also now redundant with the editor-owned invariant the lessons doc says should replace per-call-site convention — either route the panel through the heal (dropping its bespoke computation) or state the divergence deliberately in the design doc. The issue only requires "somewhere valid", so this does not fail acceptance.

`resolveCurrentSlide` notifies `currentSlideListeners` from inside `render()` / `repaintOverlay()`, and those listeners perform non-paint work: `slides-view.tsx:1073-1094` issues a Yorkie `updatePresence()` write, and `mobile-slides-view.tsx:424-428` calls React `setState`. Emitting store writes and React updates from the RAF paint path is a layering smell the diff introduces (previously only `setCurrentSlide`, a user action, fired these). A deferred/queued notification, or healing on the `store.onChange` tick, would keep paint side-effect-free. Taste/layering preference — non-blocking.

The empty-deck branch is scope beyond the issue and leaves the editor in a state the rest of the feature treats as impossible: `currentId` becomes `undefined` with no recovery, while `thumbnail-panel.ts:298-301` gates the last delete precisely because "the editor's `render()` bails out when no current slide exists, leaving a blank canvas" and slides-native-undo.md:233 asserts "A fresh deck cannot be undone back to zero slides". Tearing down anchored edits there is reasonable, but the resulting permanently-blank-deck state is undocumented and unresolved (no seed of a blank slide, no doc note). Worth either narrowing to the issue's scope or recording the intended behaviour in the slides design doc.

verdict.reason: The absence itself is real — I found no design doc anywhere under docs/design/ recording the current-slide heal invariant (resolveCurrentSlide/currentIndex appear only in packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts, the two task docs, and .agent-review/*; slides.md:564's `currentIndex` is a pre-existing interaction-table row). But it is not blocking under this lens's rubric. (1) The change is a bug fix for issue #883, not an architecture/data-model change: the task doc and lessons state the store restored the slides array correctly and only the editor's `currentId` was never revalidated; the implementation adds one private field (editor.ts:720-728) and one private method (editor.ts:1538-1574), with no model/store/public-API change (`getCurrentSlideId(): string | undefined` already existed at editor.ts:416/1500). CONTRIBUTING.md:11-12 routes bug fixes straight to a PR; the design-doc requirement at :13-16 and :57-61 is explicitly scoped to features / "Architecture / data-model changes". (2) The finding's premise that the canonical doc "states the opposite conclusion" is wrong: slides-native-undo.md:241-246 concludes post-undo dangling references are reconciled by the view layer against read() with "No store change required" — exactly what this fix does inside the editor's existing read, so no doc statement is contradicted or made stale. (3) Repo precedent: the analogous current-slide editor-state fix (docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260526-slides-toolbar-add-slide-focus-todo.md:10-25,48-61, which likewise reasons about `editor.currentId` as editor-only state) shipped with a task doc and no design-doc update. A fold-in note would be nice-to-have (minor/nit), but no required design doc is missing.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree: `resolveCurrentSlide()` (editor.ts:1538-1574) is the sole healing site for `currentId` and is reachable only from `render()` (editor.ts:1440, itself skipped by the not-dirty early return at editor.ts:1426-1433) and `repaintOverlay()` (editor.ts:1082) — i.e. paint-driven only. The editor never subscribes to its own store (no `store.onChange` anywhere in packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts). The desktop host supplies the missing tick (slides-view.tsx:1051-1052 `store.onChange → editor.markDirty()`), but the mobile edit host mounts the same editor at mobile-slides-view.tsx:376-389 with only a one-shot `editor.render()`, a ResizeObserver (:392-414) and `onCurrentSlideChange` (:424) — its `store.onChange` at :309 is inside the `mode !== "view"` read-only renderer effect (:241-325), so it does not apply to the edit mount. That mount is live and collaborative (slides-detail.tsx:738, shared-document.tsx:615), and `getCurrentSlideId()` is read eagerly there (:425, :455) and by key rules (editor.ts:1586). An eager non-paint hook is already the package idiom (layout-list-panel.ts:114). Nothing makes this unreachable or already-guarded, so the invariant is host-dependent rather than intrinsic — a placement/spec-coverage fit issue in this lane, major in kind.
